q1_issues.issue: The restrictive of-phrase is attached to the bare kind symbol `notebook`, so it asserts of notebooks at large that they are of moth-counts — a kind-level claim no word in the sentence puts there (the restriction belongs on the specific notebooks these keepers keep).
Same problem for the second conjunct: `(Of notebook weather_note)` predicates the restriction of the kind `notebook` rather than of the referents.

`CardinalityPhrase` is scoped to vague phrases that count things (a few / several / a handful / dozens / scores / hundreds / a lot of), normalized to a canonical lexicon string; "some" is an existential determiner with no listed count reading.

q2_gaps: quantity encoding for the determiner "some" over a plural — it is absent from the quantifier strength dial (all/most/a lot of/many/few/no), absent from the vague-count list, and the Existential section's "some X" case supplies only a witness, so neither a strength, a CardinalityPhrase nor a QuantifierPhrase companion is licensed for it

a content / "about" of-phrase on a non-nominalization common noun ("notebooks of moth-counts") — the genitive rule explicitly excludes about-phrases ("a photo of Mary") from Possession, and the noun has no underlying verb, so the nominalization-object oblique does not apply either; no replacement encoding is stated

a capitalized plural kind-word under a quantifier ("Some Keepers") — the capitalized-common-noun default is declared singular-collective only, while the plural branch covers only a label referring as a name ("the Wrens"), leaving a quantified capitalized plural unaddressed
notes: Group witness + group event + per-member distribution rule for a distributive predicate, and the solid-spelling/hyphenated compound decompositions (notebook→book, moth_count→count, weather_note→note, noun modifiers left unexposed), all match the instruction set. The defect is the bearer of the two `Of` atoms, not the head.
